Edit lists

Source: R/list.R
list.Rd

A list is an ordered sequence of values. Positions are 1-based. Concurrent insertions at the same position are all kept, in the same order on every replica.

  • list_insert() inserts values before the element currently at pos, and list_push() appends them. Each argument in ... becomes one element, and can be a plain value or a new container from loro_text(), loro_map(), loro_list(), and the like.

  • list_get() returns the element at pos, as a handle if it is a container.

  • list_delete() removes the elements at the positions pos, and list_clear() removes them all.

  • list_pop() removes the last element and returns it, or returns NULL if the list is empty. A removed child container is returned as its contents.

  • list_length() returns the number of elements.

A list handle also works with base functions: list[[pos]] reads like list_get(), length() is list_length(), and as.list() is container_value(). list[[pos]] = NULL removes an element like list_delete(), and for a movable list list[[pos]] = value replaces one like list_set().

A movable list, from doc_movable_list(), works with all of the functions above and adds two operations that merge cleanly across replicas. In a plain list they can only be imitated by deleting and re-inserting, which duplicates the element when two replicas do it at once.

  • list_move() moves the element at from so that it ends up at position to. Concurrent moves of one element leave a single copy.

  • list_set() replaces the element at pos in place. Concurrent sets resolve to one winner.

Plain values are converted as described in the Values section of map_set().

Usage

list_insert(list, pos, ...)

list_push(list, ...)

list_get(list, pos)

list_delete(list, pos)

list_length(list)

list_move(list, from, to)

list_set(list, pos, value)

list_pop(list)

list_clear(list)

Arguments

list

A list handle, from doc_list(), doc_movable_list(), or a parent container. list_move() and list_set() need a movable list. A loro_doc is also accepted and stands for its default root list, which is a plain list, so it cannot be used with the functions that need a movable list; see doc_text().

pos

A 1-based position. For list_delete(), a vector of positions such as 2:4.

...

Values to add, one element each: plain values or new containers. They must not be named; to store a map as one element, pass a named list or a loro_map(). These are dynamic dots, so a list of elements can be spliced in with !!!.

from, to

1-based positions.

value

A plain value or a new container.

Value

list_insert(), list_push(), list_delete(), list_clear(), list_move(), and list_set() return list invisibly. list_pop() returns the removed element. list_get() returns a value or handle, and list_length() an integer.

Examples

doc = loro_doc()
items = doc_list(doc, "items")
list_push(items, "b", "c")
list_insert(items, 1, "a")

list_push(items, loro_map(task = "d", done = FALSE))

list_get(items, 1)
#> [1] "a"
items[[2]]
#> [1] "b"
list_delete(items, 2:3)
as.list(items)
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "a"
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]]$done
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> [[2]]$task
#> [1] "d"
#> 
#> 

tasks = doc_movable_list(doc, "tasks")
list_push(tasks, "write", "test", "ship")
list_move(tasks, 3, 1)
list_set(tasks, 2, "write docs")
as.list(tasks)
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "ship"
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] "write docs"
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> [1] "test"
#>
